items.title: Circular 230 practice memo review
items.scenario: You are a senior at Halvorsen & Wu, CPAs, a firm that prepares individual and business returns. The firm's tax director drafted a memo to staff on Treasury Department Circular 230 and preparer penalties. You review it before it is distributed.
items.task: For each numbered statement in the memo, choose the option that makes the statement correct. Choose 'Keep as written' if the statement is already correct.

exhibits.title: Draft staff memo
exhibits.body:
TO: Tax staff    FROM: Tax Director    RE: Practice standards (draft)

1. When a client's prior-year depreciation schedule conflicts with this year's asset list, a practitioner who has relied on the client for years may rely on the schedule without inquiry.
2. If we learn that a client omitted income from a previously filed return, we must promptly advise the client of the omission and the consequences, but we are not required to file an amended return or notify the IRS.
3. Written informed consent for a conflict of interest must be retained and available to the IRS for at least 24 months after the representation ends.
4. A practitioner who publishes a fee schedule must adhere to the published fees for at least 90 calendar days after the last date of publication.
5. The penalty for a return-preparer understatement caused by an unreasonable position (without willful or reckless conduct) is the greater of $500 or 25% of the income derived from the return.
6. For an income tax return position that is disclosed on the return (and is not a tax shelter or reportable transaction), a preparer needs at least a reasonable basis to avoid the return-preparer penalty.

exhibits.title: Firm policy note
exhibits.body: Assume all engagements are for federal income tax return preparation by a CPA who is a practitioner under Circular 230 and a tax return preparer under the Code.

blueprint.task: Identify practitioner duties and preparer penalties

cells.label: Statement 1: reliance on client information
options: Revise: the practitioner must make reasonable inquiries when information appears incorrect, inconsistent, or incomplete
Revise: the practitioner must independently audit every client figure against source documents

cells.label: Statement 2: discovered error on a prior return
options: Revise: the practitioner must report the omission to the IRS within 30 days
Revise: the practitioner must file an amended return without the client's consent

cells.label: Statement 3: retention period for conflict-of-interest consent
Statement 5: preparer penalty amount, unreasonable position
options: Revise: the greater of $5,000 or 75% of the income derived
Revise: the greater of $1,000 or 50% of the income derived

cells.label: Statement 6: standard for a disclosed position
options: Revise: the preparer needs substantial authority even if the position is disclosed
Revise: the preparer needs a more-likely-than-not level of confidence

items.title: Secured transactions: attachment, perfection, priority
items.scenario: Tomas Appliances Inc. sells refrigerators and delivery vans in State X, which has adopted UCC Article 9. Tomas has borrowed from several lenders and sells to retail customers.
items.task: For each scenario in the exhibits, select the correct outcome.

exhibits.title: Financing history
exhibits.body:
Lender A (First Bank): security agreement covers all present and after-acquired inventory. Financing statement filed March 1, 2026.
Lender B (Coolco, a supplier): sold Tomas a new shipment of refrigerators on credit on June 10, 2026, and took a security interest in that shipment to secure the price.

exhibits.title: Scenarios
exhibits.body:
1. B filed a financing statement on June 5, and sent Lender A an authenticated notice on June 5 that it would acquire a purchase-money security interest in the refrigerators. Tomas took delivery June 10. As to the June shipment, who has priority?
2. Alternative facts: B filed its financing statement on June 15, five days after delivery, and gave no notice to A. As to the June shipment, who has priority?
3. Lena, a retail customer, bought a refrigerator from Tomas's showroom in the ordinary course of business. She knew that First Bank had a lien on Tomas's inventory. As to the refrigerator, does First Bank's security interest continue?
4. First Bank also holds a perfected security interest in a delivery van (equipment). Tomas sold the van to Sam, a friend, outside the ordinary course of business. First Bank did not authorize the sale. Does the security interest continue?
5. First Bank's financing statement was filed March 1, 2026. If no continuation statement is filed, when does perfection by that filing lapse?
6. Nia bought a $900 washing machine for personal use from Tomas on credit. Tomas retained a purchase-money security interest in it. To perfect, must Tomas file a financing statement?

blueprint.task: Determine perfection and priority

cells.label: Scenario 1: priority in the June shipment
Scenario 2: priority in the June shipment
Scenario 3: sale to a buyer in ordinary course
options: Yes, because Lena knew of the lien
Yes; First Bank can repossess the refrigerator because it is perfected
No; Lena takes free of the security interest

cells.label: Scenario 4: sale of equipment outside the ordinary course
options: No; Sam takes free because he gave value
No; the security interest is automatically terminated by any sale
Yes; the security interest continues in the van

cells.label: Scenario 5: lapse of the March 1, 2026 filing
Scenario 6: PMSI in consumer goods
options: No; a PMSI in consumer goods is automatically perfected on attachment
Yes; the seller must take possession of the washing machine
Yes; filing is the only method of perfection for consumer goods

items.title: Sales of goods under UCC Article 2
items.scenario: Northwind Supply Co. and Baker Bikes LLC are merchants in State X, which has adopted UCC Article 2. The parties exchanged several communications about a bicycle-parts purchase.
items.task: For each scenario, select the correct outcome.

exhibits.title: Facts and correspondence
exhibits.body:
1. On May 2, Baker orally agreed to buy $8,000 of parts from Northwind. On May 5 Northwind mailed a signed written confirmation to Baker. Baker received it on May 8 and did not object. Baker later refused to perform. Is the contract enforceable against Baker?
2. On June 1 Northwind gave Baker a signed writing: 'This price is good for six months.' No consideration was paid. Northwind revoked the offer on September 15. Is the revocation effective?
3. Baker's purchase order stated terms. Northwind's acknowledgment accepted but added an arbitration clause. Baker's order limited acceptance to its terms only in a sentence that was not signed. Baker did not object. Is the arbitration clause part of the contract? (Assume both are merchants and arbitration materially alters the contract.)
4. The contract was 'FOB Northwind's warehouse (shipment contract).' The goods were destroyed in transit after being delivered to the carrier in good condition, without fault of either party. Who bears the loss?
5. The parts delivered were defective in a minor way; delivery time was still open (five days remained). Baker rejected them. Can Northwind cure?
6. Ed, a neighbor who is not a merchant in lawnmowers, sold Baker his old mower for $200. Did an implied warranty of merchantability arise?

blueprint.task: Apply UCC Article 2 rules

cells.label: Scenario 1: merchant's confirmation
options: No; oral contracts for goods are never enforceable
No; there is no signed writing by Baker
Yes; the merchant confirmation satisfies the statute of frauds against Baker

cells.label: Scenario 2: firm offer
options: Yes; a firm offer is irrevocable only up to three months, and the three months had run
No; a signed writing cannot be revoked until it expires
No; the offer was irrevocable for the full six months

cells.label: Scenario 3: additional term (arbitration)
options: No; a material alteration does not become part of the contract without express assent
Yes; additional terms always become part of the contract

cells.label: Scenario 4: risk of loss in transit
Scenario 5: right to cure
options: Yes; the seller may notify the buyer and cure within the contract time
No; a cure is only allowed for a major defect
No; perfect tender means the buyer's rejection ends the contract

cells.label: Scenario 6: implied warranty of merchantability
options: Yes; every sale of goods carries the warranty
No; the seller is not a merchant with respect to goods of that kind
Yes; because the price was over $100

exhibits.title: Draft client memo
exhibits.body:
1. The filing of a bankruptcy petition automatically stays most collection actions against the debtor.
2. A trustee may avoid a preferential transfer made to a creditor within 60 days before the petition was filed (or within 12 months for an insider).
3. A debtor who receives a Chapter 7 discharge may not receive another Chapter 7 discharge in a case commenced within 4 years of the earlier case.
4. In distribution of estate assets, general unsecured creditors are paid before administrative expenses of the estate.
5. In a Chapter 11 case, a trustee must always be appointed to run the debtor's business.
6. If collateral sells for less than the secured debt, the secured creditor holds a general unsecured claim for the deficiency.

items.title: S corporation eligibility and termination: memo review
items.scenario: You are reviewing a memo written by a staff accountant to the owners of Greenfield Tools Inc., a C corporation considering an S election.
items.task: For each numbered statement, choose the option that makes the statement correct. Choose 'Keep as written' if it is already correct.

exhibits.title: Draft memo
exhibits.body:
1. An S corporation may have no more than 75 shareholders.
2. If the corporation has voting and nonvoting common stock with identical rights to distributions and liquidation proceeds, it has two classes of stock and is ineligible for S status.
3. A nonresident alien may be a shareholder of an S corporation if he or she consents to the election on Form 2553.
4. To be effective for its first tax year, the S election generally must be filed no later than the 15th day of the third month of that tax year.
5. A C corporation that converts to S status pays the built-in gains tax on gains recognized within 10 years after the conversion date.
6. An S election terminates if the corporation has accumulated earnings and profits from a C year and passive investment income above 25% of gross receipts for 2 consecutive years.

items.title: Partnership formation and operations: memo review
items.scenario: You are reviewing a memo prepared by a staff accountant for the partners of Lakeview Ventures, a newly formed general partnership that also has a limited partner.
items.task: For each numbered statement, choose the option that makes the statement correct. Choose 'Keep as written' if it is already correct.

exhibits.title: Draft memo
exhibits.body:
1. When a partner contributes appreciated property to the partnership for an interest, the partnership's basis in the property equals its fair market value on the date of contribution.
2. Guaranteed payments to a partner for services are treated as distributions and are not deductible by the partnership.
3. A partner is taxed on his or her distributive share of partnership income only when the income is distributed to the partner.
4. A current cash distribution to a partner in excess of the partner's outside basis results in gain to the partner.
5. A general partner's distributive share of ordinary business income is generally subject to self-employment tax, while a limited partner's distributive share generally is not.
6. A partner's holding period for a partnership interest received in exchange for a contributed capital asset includes the holding period of the contributed asset.

options: Revise: the partnership's basis is the FMV, but only if the property is depreciable

cells.label: Statement 2: guaranteed payments
options: Revise: guaranteed payments are capital gain to the partner
Revise: guaranteed payments are ordinary income to the partner and deductible (or capitalized) by the partnership

cells.label: Statement 3: when the partner is taxed
options: Revise: the partner is taxed on the distributive share whether or not it is distributed
Revise: the partner is taxed only on the last day of the partnership year in cash

cells.label: Statement 4: cash distribution over basis
options: Revise: the excess reduces basis below zero
Revise: the excess is taxed as ordinary income in all cases

cells.label: Statement 5: self-employment tax
options: Revise: neither is subject to self-employment tax
Revise: general partners are exempt and limited partners are subject

cells.label: Statement 6: holding period of the partnership interest
options: Revise: the holding period starts on the date of the contribution regardless of the asset
Revise: the holding period is always long-term
